Half
häf
n. and a. (one of two equal parts; in Scripture the measure of the ransom, of a divided kingdom, and of a shortened time)
From Anglo-Saxon healf, side or half — originally the side of a thing, whence the part. The older sense survives in on my half, that is, on my side, which is our behalf.

Biblical Definition

Half in Scripture is rarely a casual fraction; it is usually a deliberate measure. The atonement money is fixed at exactly “half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary” (Exo 30:13) — the rich may not give more nor the poor less, so that the ransom for a soul is the one payment in Israel where no man can outbid his brother. Half a kingdom is the extravagant royal oath, offered by Ahasuerus to Esther (Est 5:3) and by Herod to the daughter of Herodias; in both cases the half-kingdom is a king's way of saying anything, and in both cases what is actually asked exposes the asker. And half is the mark of a time cut short: “there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour” (Rev 8:1), the pause before the trumpets, and the “time, times, and an half” of Daniel and Revelation, where the broken seven signals a persecution God has measured and will not let run its full course.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines half as one equal part of a thing divided into two equal parts, and notes the older sense of side surviving in behalf.

expand to see more

HALF, n. plu. halves. One equal part of a thing which is divided into two parts, either in fact or in contemplation; a moiety.

2. It is sometimes used for a part not precisely equal, but nearly so.

HALF, a. Consisting of a moiety, or one part of two; as a half pint; a half hour.

Note. The primary sense is side; hence in behalf of, that is, on the side of.

Key Scripture

Exo 30:13 — "This they shall give, every one that passeth among them that are numbered, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary: (a shekel is twenty gerahs:) an half shekel shall be the offering of the LORD."

Est 5:3 — "Then said the king unto her, What wilt thou, queen Esther? and what is thy request? it shall be even given thee to the half of the kingdom."

Rev 8:1 — "And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour."

Exo 30:14 — "Every one that passeth among them that are numbered, from twenty years old and above, shall give an offering unto the LORD."

Modern Corruption

The half shekel is read as a temple tax like any other, when its equality is the whole doctrinal point: no man's soul is worth more than his neighbour's.

expand to see more

Exodus 30 is explicit that “the rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less than half a shekel” (Exo 30:15). Every other offering in Israel scaled with means — a bullock or a pair of turtledoves according to what a man could bring — but the ransom of a soul is fixed and identical, because the thing being ransomed is identical. Treating it as ordinary temple revenue misses that the sum is a sermon on the equal value of every image-bearer and the impossibility of any man ransoming himself by his wealth.

Psalm 49:7-8 draws the conclusion the half shekel implies: “none of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to God a ransom for him: (for the redemption of their soul is precious…)”. The half shekel was never the actual price; it was a token that a price exists, that it is the same for all, and that it would one day be paid by Another. The dividing of a thing in half in Scripture is very often a way of saying that God has set the limit and the limit holds.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chatsi (H2677), half, from chatsah, to divide; Greek hemisus (G2255), half, and the compound hemiorion (G2256), half an hour.

expand to see more

Hebrew chatsi (H2677) — half, a division; from chatsah, to cut in two, the verb used of dividing a company or a spoil.

Hebrew beqa (H1235) — the half-shekel weight itself (Exo 38:26), from a root meaning to cleave; the ransom token by name.

Greek hemisus (G2255) — half; Zacchaeus gives “the half of my goods” to the poor (Luk 19:8).

Greek hemiorion (G2256) — half an hour, used once, at the silence of Rev 8:1.

“A time, and times, and an half” (Dan 12:7; Rev 12:14) — the broken seven, a persecution measured and cut short.

Usage

"“Half a shekel” — the one offering in Israel that rich and poor pay alike."

"“To the half of the kingdom” — the royal oath that means anything, and exposes the asker."

"“The space of half an hour” — heaven's silence before the trumpets."
